risk_if_not_implemented: Without Use of FICAM-Issued Profiles, unauthorized individuals, devices or services may gain access to Technology Assets, Applications, Services, Data and/or Facilities (TAASDF). Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Loss of Authorization / Certification / License (R-EX-11), Inability to Demonstrate Due Diligence / Due Care (R-GV-9), and most likely increases susceptibility to Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Session Audit
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to provide session audit capabilities that can: 
(1) Capture and log all content related to a user session; and
(2) Remotely view all content related to an established user session in real time.
compensating_control_1.justification: Session Audit (MON-18.1) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Use of FICAM-Issued Profiles (IAC-33.5) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA)
compensating_control_2.description:
Automated mechanisms exist to enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for:
(1) Remote network access; 
(2) Third-party Technology Assets, Applications and/or Services (TAAS); and/ or
(3) Non-console access to critical TAAS that store, transmit and/or process sensitive and/or regulated data.
compensating_control_2.justification: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) (IAC-37) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Use of FICAM-Issued Profiles (IAC-33.5) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the technology-focused nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
